slides.title: prompts to find a side hustle that fits 5 hours a week
slides.sub: From your real skills to a tested offer, without quitting your job.
slides.voiceover: Here are seven prompts to find a side hustle that fits five free hours a week.

slides.name: The Skill Scanner
slides.sub: What you know that others pay for
slides.prompt: Interview me to find my sellable skills. Ask me 8 questions, one at a time, about my job, hobbies, what friends ask me for help with, and tools I use. Then list 5 skills people pay for, with **PROOF** that a market exists for each.
slides.tip: Answer honestly, even the small stuff — the skill you think is boring is usually the one people pay fastest for.
slides.voiceover: One. It interviews you and finds five skills people already pay for.

slides.name: The Hustle Matcher
slides.sub: Ideas that fit your real life
slides.prompt: Act as a career coach. My skills: [SKILLS]. I have [HOURS] hours a week, [$BUDGET] to start, and I prefer [ONLINE/OFFLINE]. Suggest 7 side hustles that fit, with startup cost, time to first income, a realistic monthly range, and the **BIGGEST RISK** of each.
slides.tip: Give it your real hours, not your hoped-for hours — a hustle that needs 15 hours will just get abandoned.
slides.voiceover: Two. It matches your skills and hours to seven real hustle ideas.

slides.name: The Reality Check
slides.sub: Kill bad ideas before they cost you
slides.prompt: Be brutally honest about this side hustle idea: [IDEA]. What does a typical beginner earn in the first 3 months, what does it really cost in time, what do most people get wrong, and what would make you say **DON'T DO IT**?
slides.tip: This one is built to disagree with you — that's the whole point of running it.
slides.voiceover: Three. It's brutally honest about what your idea really earns in month one.

slides.name: The 7-Day Test
slides.sub: Prove it with one small sale
slides.prompt: Design a 7-day experiment to test [SIDE HUSTLE] with under [$BUDGET]: day-by-day tasks under 45 minutes, the smallest offer I can sell, where to find the first 3 customers, and the number that tells me to **CONTINUE OR STOP**.

lines: Day 1-2: pick your smallest offer, price it

slides.voiceover: Four. A 7-day test that ends with a real sale, not just a plan.

slides.name: The Offer Writer
slides.sub: Say what you sell in one sentence
slides.prompt: Write my offer for [SIDE HUSTLE] for [AUDIENCE]: a one-sentence description, 3 package options with prices, what's included, the delivery time, and a short message I can send to 10 people I know **TODAY**.
slides.tip: Send the message to 10 real people before you build anything else — replies are your fastest signal.
slides.voiceover: Five. It writes your offer and a message to send ten people today.

slides.name: The Time Planner
slides.sub: Fit it around a full-time job
slides.prompt: I work [WORK HOURS] and have these free slots: [FREE TIME]. Build a weekly schedule for my side hustle [SIDE HUSTLE] that avoids burnout: which tasks go in which slot, what to automate or batch, and **ONE DAY OFF** that stays off.
slides.tip: Protect that one day off in the calendar first — everything else fits around it, not the other way.
slides.voiceover: Six. A weekly schedule that fits your job and keeps one real day off.

slides.name: The Scale Plan
slides.sub: From first sale to steady income
slides.prompt: My side hustle [SIDE HUSTLE] made [$AMOUNT] last month from [CLIENTS] clients. What should I change to reach [$GOAL] a month without doubling my hours? Cover pricing, packaging, repeat clients, and what to **STOP DOING**.
slides.tip: The "what to stop doing" line usually matters more than anything you'd add.
slides.voiceover: Seven. It turns your first sale into a real plan for steady income.
